text:
sanjay: quick check — planning a small canary in ap-southeast1 tomorrow. vendor just applied a promo credit labeled cloud_credit_2026Q1. if we spin up preemptible fallback instances will that draw down the promo or be billed separately? tagging @maria since you handle vendor ops :eyes:

maria: I asked them. short answer: credits are applied at invoice line level. depends on how the instance is classified (compute vs reservation). pinged them for definitive mapping.

kevin: FYI historically their credits offset both on-demand and preemptible compute lines. reservations sometimes show as positive then offset by a negative credit line in export. quick check you can run:```
gcloud beta billing accounts transactions list --filter=\"credit_name:cloud_credit_2026Q1\"
```

maria: vendor replied — credits map to the product code "compute" and will offset both preemptible and on-demand usage. reservations (reserved capacity) still create a reservation charge row but the credit auto-applies as a separate negative line. they said this is visible in the billing export. not sure how our internal chargeback treats the reservation row vs the credit row.

olivia: ops-bot can you surface last 7d billing rows for reservation id res-abc123? want to confirm behavior on our side.

ops-bot: (automated) found rows for res-abc123 in last 7d — 3 usage rows (total 18h), 1 credit row matching cloud_credit_2026Q1, invoice offset applied: true, net amount: -$6,432. :moneybag:

sanjay: ok good. one more: if we configure routing policy to prefer preemptible then fall back to dedicated (to keep costs down), will preemptible usage count against the promo credit when it runs, or do credits only apply to primary on-demand usage?

maria: vendor said credits apply whenever the product code is compute — so preemptible counts. they recommended tagging instances with billing_scope:promo so exports are easier to reconcile.

kevin: small terraform snippet you can use for the canary reservation and tag:```
resource \"google_compute_reservation\" \"canary\" {
  name    = \"canary-res\"
  project = \"redwood-prod\"
  specific_reservation {
    count = 2
    machine_type = \"n1-standard-8\"
  }
  labels = { billing_scope = \"promo\" }
}
```

sanjay: sweet. i'll spin up a tiny reservation (res-abc123 clone) with that label and run a 30m smoke tomorrow morning. will report results here. thanks all :thumbsup:
